# Auto-Portfolio — Implementation Details

> Implementation appendix for auto-portfolio PLAN. Contains concrete data schemas, interfaces, testing, CI, deployment, error handling, and performance budgets.

---

## 1. Serialized Data Model (site/src/data/projects.json)

This is the canonical output of the scanner. The Astro site consumes JSON files from `site/src/data/`.

```json
{
  "projects": [
    {
      "id": "repo-sha256-path",
      "name": "project-name",
      "slug": "project-name-kebab",
      "description": "Short description (<= 280 chars)",
      "long_description": "Autogenerated or README first paragraph (markdown)",
      "path": "/Users/joshua/projects/project-name",
      "remote_url": "https://github.com/you/project-name",
      "created_at": "2022-01-03T12:00:00Z",
      "last_active": "2024-04-10T16:34:00Z",
      "total_commits": 123,
      "contributors": ["you", "alice"],
      "primary_language": "TypeScript",
      "languages": {"TypeScript": 62.3, "HTML": 10.2, "CSS": 8.5},
      "stack": ["React", "Vite", "Tailwind"],
      "has_tests": true,
      "has_ci": true,
      "has_docs": true,
      "quality_score": 0.82,
      "screenshot": "public/previews/project-name.png",
      "preview_text": "A short one-line blurb",
      "tags": ["open-source","cli"],
      "size_bytes": 2456789
    }
  ]
}
```

Field notes:
- `id` must be stable across runs: use sha256(path) or repo remote URL canonicalized.
- `quality_score` is a 0-1 heuristic (docs, tests, CI, commit frequency). Stored as float for sorting.

## 2. Scanner API (core/repo_scanner.py)

```python
@dataclass
class ProjectRecord:
    id: str
    path: Path
    name: str
    slug: str
    description: str | None
    long_description: str | None
    remote_url: str | None
    created_at: datetime
    last_active: datetime
    total_commits: int
    contributors: list[str]
    primary_language: str
    languages: dict[str, float]
    stack: list[str]
    has_tests: bool
    has_ci: bool
    has_docs: bool
    quality_score: float
    tags: list[str]
    screenshot_path: Path | None
    size_bytes: int

class RepoScanner:
    def scan_root(self, root: Path) -> List[ProjectRecord]:
        """Walk directory tree (respecting exclude patterns) and return project records."""
    def scan_repo(self, repo_path: Path) -> ProjectRecord:
        """Single-repo extraction. Deterministic and resumable."""
    def detect_stack(self, repo_path: Path) -> list[str]: ...
    def language_distribution(self, repo_path: Path) -> dict[str,float]: ...
    def commit_metrics(self, repo_path: Path) -> tuple[int, list[str], datetime, datetime]: ...
    def read_readme(self, repo_path: Path) -> str | None: ...
```

Implementation details:
- Use `git` command for speed (avoid building entire GitPython objects for large repos). Example commands:
  - `git -C path rev-list --count HEAD` for commit count
  - `git -C path log -n 1 --format=%cI` for last commit date
  - `git -C path log --pretty=format:%an | sort -u` for contributors
- Language distribution: use `cloc` or a simple file-extension heuristic (fast) with caching per repo (hash of HEAD ref)
- For manifests: parse `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `Gemfile` exactly once per scan; prefer manifest detection over file extension heuristics.

Caching:
- Cache results under `~/.cache/auto-portfolio/<repo-id>/<head-sha>.json` to make incremental runs near-instant.
- Invalidate cache on HEAD change.

---

## 3. Description Generation (core/description_gen.py)

Strategy:
1. Prefer README top paragraph (first non-empty paragraph). If > 280 chars, truncate to sentence boundary.
2. If README absent or too terse, use an LLM (local Ollama or API) with a prompt that includes:
   - repo name
   - top 10 commit messages
   - detected stack
   - first 300 lines of important files (package.json, main module)
3. Keep a local audit log of generated descriptions for human review (`data/generated_descriptions.jsonl`).

LLM prompt constraints:
- No network unless allowed by config
- Max 512 tokens context (prioritize README + commits + manifest)
- Temperature: 0.0 for deterministic outputs

---

## 4. Asset Builder (core/asset_builder.py)

Responsibilities:
- Generate a preview screenshot for each project
- Produce a favicon and palette derived from codebase or avatar

Screenshot strategies:
- If repo already has a `screenshot.png` or `docs/preview.png`, use it.
- Otherwise, attempt headless rendering:
  1. If web dev server available (package.json scripts with `start`), start dev server in headless mode using `pnpm`/`npm run start -- --port $RANDOM` or `vite preview`.
  2. Use Playwright to load `http://localhost:$PORT` and take a responsive screenshot (mobile + desktop variants).
  3. If starting dev server fails or app is backend-only, render an auto-generated image:
     - Use a template card with project name, tags, and a subtle generated background based on primary language color.

Playwright details:
- `playwright` managed via `playwright` Python package or through node-playwright (prefers node for ecosystem parity).
- Timeouts: 15s startup, 10s page load. Keep headless and sandboxed.
- Cleanup: ensure server process is killed even on error (use process group).

Favicon & palette:
- Use `dominant-color` algorithm on screenshot to derive accent color.
- Generate favicon sizes (32x32, 180x180) using Pillow.

---

## 5. Site Generation (site/)

Astro + Tailwind setup (opinionated):
- Use Astro v4+, Tailwind v4, and minimal JS on pages.
- Data files placed in `site/src/data/projects.json` and consumed at build time.

Build optimizations:
- Precompute screenshots and images into `site/public/previews/`.
- Avoid heavy JS: keep interaction minimal and rely on pre-rendered HTML.
- Use `astro build` for static output. For incremental builds, implement a small makefile that re-generates only changed pages by writing individual JSON files per project and importing them via dynamic `import.meta.glob`.

SEO & Accessibility:
- Generate `og:image` for each project using the preview image.
- Ensure all images have `alt` attributes.
- Use semantic markup and ARIA where needed.

---

## 6. Testing Strategy

Unit tests:
- `tests/unit/test_scanner.py` — mock `git` outputs and manifests to test detection logic
- `tests/unit/test_description_gen.py` — test LLM prompt fallback and safety truncation
- `tests/unit/test_asset_builder.py` — simulate servers and verify screenshot fallback
- `tests/unit/test_models.py` — pydantic validation, slugging, ID stability

Integration tests:
- `tests/integration/test_generate_site.py` — run a small sample repo list, generate `projects.json`, run `npm run build` in `site/`, verify built HTML contains expected project slugs
- `tests/integration/test_playwright` — run Playwright headless flow against a tiny sample site

E2E/Smoke:
- `tests/e2e/test_deploy_preview` — generate site and serve locally (npm serve), fetch home page and assert status 200

Fixtures:
- `tests/fixtures/sample_repo/` (with package.json, basic index.html)
- `tests/fixtures/backend_repo/` (no web UI) to assert fallback image generation

Coverage targets:
- Core 90%+, Asset builder 80%+, Site generation 80%

## 7. CI/CD (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

```yaml
name: Auto-Portfolio CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: '3.12'}
      - run: python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
      - run: python -m pytest -q

  build_site:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: cd site && npm ci && npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site-dist
          path: site/dist/

  deploy:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build_site
    steps:
      - name: Download site
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: {name: site-dist}
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4
        with:
          deploy_key: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
          publish_dir: ./site-dist
```

---

## 8. Deployment Targets

1. GitHub Pages: simplest for static site. Use `gh-pages` branch. Use `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages` to upload `site/dist`.
2. Vercel: better for preview deployments. Use Vercel CLI in CI with token. Advantage: preview URLs per PR.
3. Netlify: similar to Vercel. Choose one as user preference in config.

Rollback plan:
- Keep `site-dist` artifacts in CI. A rollback simply re-deploys a previous artifact.
- Use semantic versioning for releases and tag generated site artifacts.

---

## 9. Error Handling

- If Playwright screenshot fails: log error, fallback to generated title card image.
- If manifest parse fails: ignore that manifest and fallback to file-extension detection.
- If `git` commands fail due to permissions: skip repo and include it in `skipped_repos.log` for user review.
- If LLM generation fails or times out: fall back to README-based approach.
- Always run in `--dry-run` by default unless `--confirm` passed for destructive operations (not many destructive operations here).

---

## 10. Performance Budgets

| Operation | Target |
|----------|--------|
| Scan 50 small repos (cached) | < 3s |
| Full scan (cold) | < 20s for 50 repos |
| Playwright screenshot per app (start + render) | < 12s (target) |
| Site build (Astro) | < 12s for 50 projects |
| Homepage render (static) | < 500ms LCP |

Profiling tips:
- Use HEAD-based caching to avoid re-scanning unchanged repos.
- Parallelize asset generation (concurrency limited to CPU/IO bound values) but keep Playwright concurrency low to avoid system pressure.

---

## 11. Security & Privacy

- All scanning and LLM operations default to local-only. External API calls must be explicitly enabled.
- Do not upload private repo contents to 3rd-party LLMs without explicit consent. Provide `--allow-llm-remote` flag for users to opt-in.
- Store any generated artifacts under `~/.cache/auto-portfolio/` or project's `site/public/previews/` only.
- If remote deployment is configured, allow the user to redact sensitive fields (e.g., remote_url) in `config.toml`.

---

## 12. Observability & Telemetry

- Local structured logs in `~/.cache/auto-portfolio/log.jsonl` for debugging.
- Health check CLI `auto-portfolio health` that reports last scan time, cache hit rate, pending assets.
- Optional telemetry: anonymized usage metrics (opt-in only) — how many repos scanned, errors encountered. Use a hashed machine-id and provide `--telemetry disable`.

---

## 13. Migration & Versioning

- Maintain a `schema_version` file in `site/src/data/` and update it when data model changes.
- Implement `auto-portfolio migrate` command to upgrade cached data to the new schema.

---

## 14. Developer Experience

- `auto-portfolio setup` creates a `config.toml` and installs optional Playwright browsers.
- `auto-portfolio generate --watch` will watch the given paths and rebuild changed project JSONs and preview images automatically.
- Developer mode: `AUTO_PORTFOLIO_DEBUG=1 auto-portfolio generate` enables verbose logging and dumps intermediate cache for inspection.
